recent_transactions.rationale: ADD (corporate action, non-cash, not a watchlist-screened buy): Gentherm Incorporated (THRM) shares received as part of Modine's (MOD) Reverse Morris Trust spin-merger of its Performance Technologies segment into Gentherm, which closed 2026-10-01 (record date 9/28) -- 0.44619 THRM shares distributed per MOD share held. This was missed by prior daily reviews; discovered today while investigating MOD's continued price decline, which turns out to be substantially explained by the spin-off's value transfer (MOD dropped ~10% intraday on the 9/28 ex-date) rather than generic 'AI-data-center-adjacent/industrials weakness' as previously assumed. The retained Modine entity keeps the Data Centers/Commercial HVAC (Climate Solutions) business the original position's AI-cooling thesis was built on; Performance Technologies (lower-growth legacy automotive/industrial segment) is what was divested, so the retained MOD thesis is arguably sharpened, not broken. No official IRS Form 8937 cost-basis split was located; MOD's original $184.86/share cost basis was reallocated between MOD and these new THRM shares using the relative-fair-value method (first post-distribution regular-way closing prices on 10/1: MOD $189.21, THRM $31.56), yielding new cost bases of MOD $172.05/share and THRM $28.70/share -- see portfolio.json for detail. No cash impact (price shown is today's market price for reference only, not an acquisition cost). Token-sized (~0.05% of portfolio); doesn't move any sizing/sector/opportunity-bucket cap.

Dedicated research check found no October-specific news, good or bad: the known customer-concentration risk flagged at the 10/14 add (top 4 customers ~82% of Q2 revenue per the Q2 10-Q) remains disclosed and stable, not worsening, and the stock's recent weakness reads as the broader sector-wide chip selloff (hitting CRDO/peers too) rather than a company-specific issue. Fundamentals intact: Q2'26 revenue $392M (>2x YoY, beat), Q3 guided to $540-560M (~40% QoQ). Passed on five higher-scoring candidates on this screen, each disqualified for a specific, dated reason: ASTS (still no news addressing the 10/13 Piper Sandler SpaceX-competitive-threat downgrade that triggered our 10/16 exit -- re-buy restriction stands), RCAT (CRO retaliation lawsuit from the 7/21 for-cause termination remains unresolved, no October update), SERV (Uber Eats non-renewal now confirmed executed -- Grubhub/DoorDash diversification is real but FY26 guidance cut to $9-10M stands, stock down ~45% over the past year), ZENA (a fresh October 2026 Form 424B5 offering at $1.35/share confirms, rather than resolves, the dilution concern flagged at the 10/14 pass), and IONQ (no news since 10/14 addressing the Elisity-deal/dilutive-raise strategic-drift concern behind our 10/14 exit; the ~35.8M new shares for Elisity, ~9% of shares out, confirm the dilution is material). Also passed on NVDA, which clears on fundamentals (105.9% revenue growth, 127.8% earnings growth, forward P/E 13.9, no negative catalyst found) but is the familiar mega-cap -- per the mandate against defaulting to blue chips over a smaller name the screen ranked higher without a specific reason, preferring ALAB here since nothing in the research disqualifies it. Not opportunity-tier; sized to the available cash above the 2% buffer floor ($54.16), the binding constraint today (ample remaining room in both the Technology sector cap and the 15% position cap).

Fundamentals data (market cap, revenue/earnings growth) is unavailable this run -- yfinance's quoteSummary endpoint returned 401 Unauthorized/Invalid Crumb for all 91 tracked tickers today, a full fundamentals-API outage, not specific to this decision. No earnings miss, guidance cut, or litigation; Q2 organic-growth guidance was actually raised to a 20-22% CAGR target through 2030, and sell-side remains heavily bullish (83% buy-rated, ~$341 average PT, GLJ upgrade to Buy $381). Trimming 30% to de-risk specifically because the 9/9 $1.45B UtilityInnovation Group acquisition still has undisclosed target financials and the Massachusetts data-center permitting order remains an unresolved overhang layered on top of the high beta -- not a full exit since there is no thesis-breaking catalyst.
